NEWS 


FROM THE MONTREAL YMCA 


1441 DRUMMOND ST., MONTREAL 
TELEPHONE 849-5331, EXT. 57 


March 30th, 1965 
STUDENT ACTIVITIES PLAY VITAL 


ROLE IN MODERN EDUCATION 


Magnus Flynn, Dean of Students of Sir George Williams University, 
speaking to the first report luncheon of the current Y.M.C.A. 
financial campaign stressed the vital role of student affairs 


in modern education. 


"The trend to large classes, and the depersonalization of 
growing student bodies has made the co-curricular program of 
students an essential element of the educational process", said 
Mr. Flynn. "Years ago these student activities were largely re- 
creational and often suspected of diverting the student from 
his real purpose in attending university. Today we recognize 
that assuming responsibility for the leadership of student 
clubs, and taking part in many phases of university life, gives 
students practical ways of expressing their concerns and 


developing their own leadership abilities." 


Mr. Flynn spoke of the tremendous contribution that the student 
government is making to the university.and commended the Y.M.C.A. 
for its support in providing the staff and facilities for a 


growing program of student leader training.

Bob Hoppe, Chairman of the Y's 1965 Campaign heard reports 
from the fifteen Divisional Chairmen totalling $ 73,209 or 
23.6% of the 310,000 objective. The Westmount Division topped 


the reports with 39.1% of its local objective. 


Other leading divisions were: Northmount 28.3% and St. Andrews 
27 02s 


J. Leonard Walker, Chairman of the Special Names Division 


reported $ 48,289 to date for the 25% of its objective. 


The Y campaign will continue until April 12th.
